The patient's phenotype — BCGitis, reduced MHC II cell surface expression, recurrent infections (pneumonia, otitis media), lymphadenitis, splenomegaly, decreased B cells, failure to thrive, protracted diarrhea, cellulitis — is classic for MHC class II deficiency (Bare Lymphocyte Syndrome type II). None of the provided literature chunks directly name any of these genes as causing MHC II deficiency. However, reasoning from known biology: CD72 is a B-cell co-receptor/regulator with direct relevance to B-cell counts and immune function, and its chunk has the highest critic_relevance score (4/5) with direct mention. The remaining genes have no specific evidence linking them to this phenotype. Given the hallmark "Reduced MHC II cell surface expression" combined with BCGitis and decreased B cells, the closest known genes are CIITA, RFX5, RFXANK, RFXAP — none of which are in the candidate list. Among candidates, CD72 has the most relevant immunological evidence. All others are essentially equally unsupported by the provided evidence.
